big_idea: We can sort by TWO rules at once. Venn and Carroll diagrams show overlap.
learning_intention: We are learning to sort by two attributes using Venn or Carroll.
student_learning_goal: I can sort by two attributes using Venn or Carroll.
success_criteria: I can place items in a Venn diagram (with overlap!).
I can use a Carroll diagram (yes/no x yes/no).
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dot and Tally — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Detective Dot: This time I sort by TWO rules! Red AND square — overlap! Carroll table — red AND not-square... Detective Dot opens: 'BOTH? Only one? Or NEITHER?' (Class echoes.)
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dot and Tally puppets. 'Friends — last year you sorted by ONE rule. Today we sort by TWO RULES at once.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write VENN DIAGRAM and CARROLL DIAGRAM on chart. 'Venn = 2 overlapping circles. Carroll = 2x2 yes/no table.'

Demo Venn. Draw 2 circles overlapping. 'Left = RED. Right = SQUARE. OVERLAP = red AND square. Outside = neither.'

Place cards: red triangle (left), blue square (right), red square (overlap), blue triangle (outside).

Demo Carroll. Draw 2x2 table.
      | RED | NOT RED
SQUARE| RS  | NS
NOT SQ| RNS | Other

Place same cards: red square in 'red+square' cell, blue square in 'not-red+square' cell, etc.

'Detective Dot says — Venn is for OVERLAP. Carroll is for YES/NO splits.'

'Today we sort 30 cards two ways.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: sort 4 cards by 2 attributes (red/blue × square/triangle).
Three stations. Station A: Venn — sort 12 cards. Station B: Carroll — same 12 cards. Station C: Pick own 2 attributes.
Stretch challenge at Station C: 3-attribute sort.
Discuss when to use Venn vs Carroll. 'Venn when overlap. Carroll when clear yes/no.'

steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their Venn vs Carroll sorts of the same set. Class debates: which makes overlap obvious? Which makes 'neither' obvious? Cite Inhelder & Piaget (1964) and English (1993) on cross-classification — Venn highlights intersection, Carroll grids highlight complete coverage.
steps.teacher_prompt: Detective Dot: 'Same shapes, two displays. Each one tells a different STORY.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use only 8 cards.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children stand in 2 hula hoops on the floor; some in overlap zone.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: picks 2 attributes; places in Venn correctly; places in Carroll correctly.

discussion_prompts: Dot's preview: tomorrow Tally turns today's two-attribute thinking into a TWO-WAY TALLY TABLE (Lesson 2 — D1.1). What would the rows and columns be?
consolidation.exit_routine: Detective Dot's 4-zone refrain — class chants: 'BOTH? Only one? Or NEITHER?' (3x). Each child writes one shape + zone on a sticky.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Two-attribute sorting with Venn and Carroll.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 surfaces children who already use 2-attribute sorting.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child puts cards ONLY in the overlap (or NEVER in the overlap) — repairing the all-or-none-overlap trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On two-rule sorting (Venn / Carroll), the dominant Grade-2 trap is the cross-classification difficulty: pre-stage-III children track ONE attribute at a time and resist the INTERSECTION (Inhelder & Piaget 1964 'The Early Growth of Logic in the Child'; English 1993 'Children's Strategies in Solving Two- and Three-Dimensional Combinatorial Problems'). Without intersection fluency, Lesson 2's two-way tally tables cannot ground.

Today: sort by TWO rules at once. Tomorrow Tally turns the same two-attribute thinking into a TWO-WAY tally TABLE (Lesson 2 — D1.1). Lesson 3 reads bar graphs; Lesson 4 finds mode; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Venn with red/square circles. Child puts all 12 cards in the overlap zone, even blue triangles.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Wait — overlap is for cards that are BOTH red AND square. This blue triangle is NEITHER.'

Walk through. 'Outside circles = neither. Left only = red AND not-square. Right only = square AND not-red. Overlap = BOTH.'

Generlise. 'Detective Dot says — overlap is for cards with BOTH attributes.'

Now re-sort. Pull cards out, place one at a time: 'red triangle = left only. Blue square = right only. Red square = overlap. Blue triangle = outside.'

If still confused: provide a 4-zone label sticker. 'left only / right only / both / neither.'

Long-term recovery: every Venn names all 4 zones.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Puts all in overlap or none.
(Stretched) Predicts which cards go where before sorting.
common_misconceptions: Overlap = default. (Repair: overlap = BOTH attributes only.)
Outside circles = lost. (Repair: outside = neither attribute.)
Carroll and Venn are interchangeable. (Repair: Carroll has yes/no, Venn has overlap.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child puts ALL in overlap zone: drill 'NEITHER' and 'ONLY-ONE' zones with non-examples; child labels each shape by zone before placing.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child cannot articulate why a shape goes in overlap: physical demo — hold one attribute in each hand (red? big?); child says 'YES + YES = overlap.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child sorts by one rule then re-sorts by the other: keep both rule cards visible; child checks both cards before placing each shape.

parts_outline.task: Place 6 items in a Venn diagram (red circle, square circle).
Same 6 items in a Carroll diagram.
Pick 2 attributes for 4 of your toys. Make either Venn or Carroll.
